All Rustwurk has been is a forum.

Messages.Author: James Coupe
Messages.Body:
In message <3e15ab98....@netnews.attbi.com>,
berni...@attbi.comHOLDLeSPAM writes:
<Online V:TES resources, a la Rustwurk>

>I respectfully disagree with you on this Jeff. By all rights White
>Wolf's Vampire CCG page should be THE central internet hub.

In part, that depends on what the function of such a hub is.

Were V:TES a huge, sprawling, disparate subject like, say, Unix
operating systems, you'd have significant problems stuffing everything
into one hub - the intersection of device driver programming, web
scripting, kernel details, how to run the latest game and so on isn't
that huge, since lots of people will want one bit and not another.
V:TES is generally much more focused than that.

A central hub is much more likely to include a lot more of the
information lots of people want/need. Lasombra's website does such now,
for instance.

Where does this cause problems? For a start, lots of people want card
lists *as soon as the cards become available*. With small sets, these
are often rapidly constructed, well in advance of White Wolf releasing
them. Would it then be appropriate for White Wolf to be hosting the
unofficial ones as well? Such could be problematic - a number of
promotional things done with magazines often work on the principal that
the company won't release the information. Hosting the unofficial ones
too has problems.

So then you have the problem of them having to weed out some things, and
it ceases to be a central hub, but one of several.

Similar problems might occur if, say, White Wolf go temporarily insane,
sack LSJ, double the price of V:TES cards, employ 5 year old children to
colour them in by hand in sweat shops and rule that half your collection
is unplayable on different days.[0] A central hub would be a good place
for different groups of players to put their views forward, and campaign
in certain ways. Again, having it on a White Wolf administered server
could cause problems.

Additionally, designing, maintaining and promoting such a hub introduces
additional costs for White Wolf. Now, we know that some post-WotC V:TES
cards have sold like crack cocaine *but* we don't know what the profit
margin is like. I'd guess somewhere between okay and respectable - bear
in mind that the cost of V:TES isn't that hugely different to the cost
of similar sets in Magic or Harry Potter or Pokemon or similar, but they
gain in terms of economies of scale, huge muscle with printing firms or
whatever. Employing person/people to maintain a rapidly changing,
extensive web-site isn't done with peanuts, unfortunately, whereas
player-run sites a) keep players more in touch with each other and b)
are free.

Cynical? Me?

[0] Suggestion obviously extreme. However, more down to earth problems
might be protests against 7/7 rulings, the grouping rule or whatever.

--

Joshua Duffin wrote:

> But seriously, it's true that there's some intelligent discussion
> on Usenet, but there could be *so* much more.

You are correct, sir!

> A useful "central
> gathering place" website might capture some, and good editors
> could make sure that the content was of a quality to be useful
> and to attract more good content from readers.

It certainly could be, but you are always going to have some folks who don't
want to read web forums, some people who don't want to read USENET, and some
who don't wan't to read both.

However, as a reasonable example, the Star Fleet Battles internet community
used to be spread around USENET (on rec.games.board) and various listserves,
but then a few years ago (4? 5?), the game company started up their own BBS,
which is where *all* of the SFB internet discussion exists at this point,
and it is both very well organized and full of solid, intelligent
discussion. But then the game designers (Cole and Petrick) run the place
with a pair of iron fists, and won't tollerate *any* internet foolishness
(i.e. any flame wars are shut down with extreme predudice and removal of
posting priveleges, and misplaced or inappropriate discussion is
extinguished quickly). That, and the mean age of SFB players is probably,
like, 30, so there is much less, shall we say, youthfull inexperience. So it
is certainly possible to have a solid, accessible web hub for discussion and
such, but I suspect it takes a lot of work and very focused moderators.
